class CeurSemantifyCmd(BaseCmd):
    """
    command line interface of pyCEURsemantify:
    generate volume pages, rebuild year pages, serve the endpoint
    """

    def __init__(self):
        """
        constructor
        """
        super().__init__(Version())

    def add_arguments(self, parser: ArgumentParser) -> None:
        """
        add the arguments to the given parser

        Args:
            parser: the argument parser
        """
        super().add_arguments(parser)
        parser.add_argument(
            "volumes",
            nargs="*",
            help="volume numbers and ranges to generate, e.g. 3889 3887-3912",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "-y",
            "--year",
            type=int,
            action="append",
            dest="years",
            help="rebuild the page of the given year from the volumes present (can be given several times)",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--regenerate",
            action="store_true",
            help="with --year: fetch and write the volumes present for the year again before rebuilding its page",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--embed",
            nargs="+",
            metavar="PATH",
            help="embed the JSON-LD into the given volume pages of the proceedings chairs (index.html files or"
            " volume directories) and write index.jsonld next to them",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--generate",
            nargs="+",
            metavar="PATH",
            help="generate the volume and paper pages from the given local volume pages (index.html files or"
            " volume directories, an embedded page is read from its index.jsonld) instead of ceur-spt",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--in-place",
            action="store_true",
            help="with --generate: write the volume page, its index.jsonld and the paper pages into the volume"
            " directory itself instead of the year tree of the output directory; the volume page is overwritten",
        )
        parser.add_argument("--progress", action="store_true", help="show a progress bar while generating volumes")
        parser.add_argument(
            "--serve",
            action="store_true",
            help="load all JSON-LD files into memory and serve them as SPARQL endpoint",
        )
        parser.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1", help="host of the endpoint (default: %(default)s)")
        parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=9987, help="port of the endpoint (default: %(default)s)")
        parser.add_argument(
            "-o",
            "--output",
            default=".",
            help="directory that holds the year directories (default: current directory)",
        )
        parser.add_argument("--config", help="site configuration yaml file (default: the packaged site.yaml)")

    def show_report(self, title: str, report: SiteReport, args: Namespace) -> None:
        """
        show the given report: problems always, written files if verbose

        Args:
            title: what the report is about
            report: the report
            args: the parsed arguments
        """
        for problem in report.problems:
            print(problem, file=sys.stderr)
        if args.verbose:
            for path in report.written:
                print(path)
        if not args.quiet:
            print(f"{title}: {len(report.written)} files, {len(report.problems)} problems, {report.seconds:.1f} s")

    def handle_args(self, args: Namespace) -> bool:
        """
        handle the parsed arguments

        Args:
            args: the parsed arguments

        Returns:
            bool: True if the arguments were handled
        """
        handled = super().handle_args(args)
        if not handled:
            config = SiteConfig.of_yaml(args.config)
            generator = Generator.of_output(args.output, config)
            if args.embed:
                report = generator.embed_volumes(args.embed, progress=args.progress)
                self.show_report(f"{len(args.embed)} volume pages", report, args)
                handled = True
            if args.generate:
                report = generator.generate_paths(args.generate, progress=args.progress, in_place=args.in_place)
                self.show_report(f"{len(args.generate)} volume pages", report, args)
                handled = True
            if args.volumes:
                numbers = VolumeRanges.numbers(args.volumes)
                report = generator.generate_volumes(numbers, progress=args.progress)
                self.show_report(f"{len(numbers)} volumes", report, args)
                handled = True
            for year in args.years or []:
                if args.regenerate:
                    report = generator.regenerate_year(year, progress=args.progress)
                else:
                    report = generator.rebuild_year(year)
                self.show_report(f"year {year}", report, args)
                handled = True
            if args.serve:
                endpoint = SptEndpoint(generator.site)
                load_report = endpoint.load()
                if not args.quiet:
                    print(
                        f"endpoint: {load_report.files} files, {load_report.triples} triples, "
                        f"{load_report.seconds:.1f} s, http://{args.host}:{args.port}/npq/{endpoint.name}"
                    )
                endpoint.serve(host=args.host, port=args.port)
                handled = True
        return handled

class Convert:
    """
    conversions of source values to the values of the research model

    Each conversion is named in resources/ceurspt_mapping.yaml and raises a
    ValueError for a value it can not convert.
    """

    @classmethod
    def text(cls, value: Any) -> str:
        """
        normalize whitespace: line breaks and runs of blanks become one blank

        Args:
            value: the source text

        Returns:
            str: the single line text
        """
        text = " ".join(str(value).split())
        return text

    @classmethod
    def integer(cls, value: Any) -> int:
        """
        convert the given value to an integer

        Args:
            value: the source value

        Returns:
            int: the integer
        """
        integer = int(value)
        return integer

    @classmethod
    def volume_number(cls, value: Any) -> int:
        """
        get the volume number of a volume identifier such as Vol-3889

        Args:
            value: the volume identifier

        Returns:
            int: the volume number
        """
        match = re.fullmatch(r"Vol[-.]?(\d+)", str(value).strip())
        if not match:
            raise ValueError(f"not a volume identifier: {value}")
        volume_number = int(match.group(1))
        return volume_number

    @classmethod
    def iso_date(cls, value: Any) -> str:
        """
        check that the given value is an ISO date

        Args:
            value: the source date

        Returns:
            str: the date as YYYY-MM-DD
        """
        iso_date = date.fromisoformat(str(value).strip()).isoformat()
        return iso_date

    @classmethod
    def last_path_parts(cls, value: Any, marker: str) -> str:
        """
        get the part of the path of an url that follows the given marker

        Args:
            value: the url or an identifier without url
            marker: the path segment the identifier follows e.g. /pid/

        Returns:
            str: the identifier
        """
        identifier = str(value).strip()
        path = urlparse(identifier).path
        if marker in path:
            identifier = path.split(marker, 1)[1]
        return identifier

    @classmethod
    def wikidata_id(cls, value: Any) -> str:
        """
        get the Q-identifier of a Wikidata entity url or identifier

        Args:
            value: the entity url or Q-identifier

        Returns:
            str: the Q-identifier
        """
        wikidata_id = cls.last_path_parts(value, "/entity/")
        if not re.fullmatch(r"Q\d+", wikidata_id):
            raise ValueError(f"not a Wikidata identifier: {value}")
        return wikidata_id

    @classmethod
    def dblp_person_id(cls, value: Any) -> str:
        """
        get the dblp person identifier of a dblp person url

        Args:
            value: the url e.g. https://dblp.org/pid/32/7870

        Returns:
            str: the identifier e.g. 32/7870
        """
        dblp_person_id = cls.last_path_parts(value, "/pid/")
        return dblp_person_id

    @classmethod
    def dblp_record_id(cls, value: Any) -> str:
        """
        get the dblp publication identifier of a dblp record url

        Args:
            value: the url e.g. https://dblp.org/rec/conf/semtab/X24

        Returns:
            str: the identifier e.g. conf/semtab/X24
        """
        dblp_record_id = cls.last_path_parts(value, "/rec/")
        return dblp_record_id

    @classmethod
    def file_stem(cls, value: Any) -> str:
        """
        get the file name without extension of an url

        Args:
            value: the url e.g. https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3889/paper0.pdf

        Returns:
            str: the stem e.g. paper0
        """
        path = urlparse(str(value)).path
        file_stem = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(path))[0]
        if not file_stem:
            raise ValueError(f"no file name in: {value}")
        return file_stem

    @classmethod
    def page_part(cls, value: Any, index: int) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        get the first or last page of a page range such as 1-11

        Args:
            value: the page range or a single page
            index: 0 for the first page, -1 for the last page

        Returns:
            Optional[str]: the page
        """
        parts = [part.strip() for part in re.split(r"[-–—]+", str(value)) if part.strip()]
        if not parts:
            raise ValueError(f"no pages in: {value}")
        page_part = parts[index]
        return page_part

    @classmethod
    def page_start(cls, value: Any) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        get the first page of a page range

        Args:
            value: the page range

        Returns:
            Optional[str]: the first page
        """
        page_start = cls.page_part(value, 0)
        return page_start

    @classmethod
    def page_end(cls, value: Any) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        get the last page of a page range

        Args:
            value: the page range

        Returns:
            Optional[str]: the last page
        """
        page_end = cls.page_part(value, -1)
        return page_end

        str: the Q-identifier
    """
    wikidata_id = cls.last_path_parts(value, "/entity/")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"Q\d+", wikidata_id):
        raise ValueError(f"not a Wikidata identifier: {value}")

class EarlyVolumeHtml(VolumeHtml):
    """
    an early volume page without the CEUR marks of the volume template
    """

    # longest first so that .ps.gz is not taken as .gz
    document_extensions = [".ps.gz", ".pdf", ".ps"]
    # the elements that hold one entry of the table of contents
    entry_elements = ["li", "tr", "p", "dd", "dt"]

    def document_of(self, href: Optional[str]) -> Optional[Tuple[str, str]]:
        """
        get the stem and extension of a link to a document of the volume itself

        Args:
            href: the href of the link

        Returns:
            Optional[Tuple[str, str]]: the stem and the extension, None for
                other links and for documents outside the volume
        """
        document = None
        if href:
            href = href.strip()
            if not urlparse(href).scheme and "/" not in href.strip("./"):
                name = posixpath.basename(href)
                for extension in self.document_extensions:
                    if name.lower().endswith(extension):
                        document = (name[: -len(extension)], extension)
                        break
        return document

    def title_of(self, link: Tag) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        get the title of the paper the given link belongs to

        Args:
            link: the link to the document of the paper

        Returns:
            Optional[str]: the text of the entry when it holds only this paper,
                the link text otherwise
        """
        entry = link.find_parent(self.entry_elements)
        title = None
        if entry is not None:
            stems = {self.document_of(a.get("href"))[0] for a in entry.find_all("a") if self.document_of(a.get("href"))}
            if len(stems) == 1:
                title = Convert.text(entry.get_text()) or None
        if title is None:
            title = Convert.text(link.get_text()) or None
        return title

    def papers(self, url: str, result: MappingResult) -> List[Paper]:
        """
        get the papers of the volume: every document of the volume itself
        the page links, one paper per file stem in the order of the page

        Args:
            url: the url of the volume
            result: the mapping result to report issues to

        Returns:
            List[Paper]: the papers, the pdfUrl is the official PDF also when
                only a PostScript file exists, see https://github.com/ceurws/semantify/issues/39
        """
        links: Dict[str, Tag] = {}
        extensions: Dict[str, set] = {}
        for link in self.soup.find_all("a"):
            document = self.document_of(link.get("href"))
            if document is not None:
                stem, extension = document
                links.setdefault(stem, link)
                extensions.setdefault(stem, set()).add(extension)
        papers = []
        for stem, link in links.items():
            title = self.title_of(link)
            if title is None:
                result.issues.append(MappingIssue("Paper", stem, "no title"))
            if ".pdf" not in extensions[stem]:
                result.issues.append(MappingIssue("Paper", stem, "PostScript only"))
            paper = Paper(id=stem, title=title, pdfUrl=urljoin(url, f"{stem}.pdf"), publishedIn=url, authors=[])
            papers.append(paper)
        return papers

    def volume_number_of(self, result: MappingResult) -> Optional[int]:
        """
        get the volume number from the Vol-N of the path, the page has no CEURVOLNR
        see https://github.com/ceurws/semantify/issues/37
        """
        return self.volume_number

class Embedder:
    """
    embed the JSON-LD into the volume page of the proceedings chair: the
    state comment before the html element, the alternate link and the fence
    in the head; the markup of the chair is otherwise untouched
    """

    alternate_link = '<link rel="alternate" type="application/ld+json" href="index.jsonld">'
    state_pattern = re.compile(r"<!-- CEURSTATE=[^\n]*? -->\n?")
    fence_pattern = re.compile(rf"<!--\n{Fence.fence}json-ld\n.*?\n{Fence.fence}\n-->\n?", re.DOTALL)
    link_pattern = re.compile(re.escape(alternate_link) + r"\n?")
    # the state comment goes after the doctype, before the html element otherwise
    doctype_pattern = re.compile(r"<!DOCTYPE[^>]*>\n?", re.IGNORECASE)
    html_pattern = re.compile(r"<html[\s>]", re.IGNORECASE)
    head_pattern = re.compile(r"<head[^>]*>\n?", re.IGNORECASE)

    def __init__(self, state: PageState):
        """
        constructor

        Args:
            state: the state the page announces
        """
        self.state = state

    def strip(self, html_text: str) -> str:
        """
        remove the embedded parts from the given page

        Args:
            html_text: the html of a volume page

        Returns:
            str: the html without state comment, alternate link and fence
        """
        stripped = self.state_pattern.sub("", html_text)
        stripped = self.fence_pattern.sub("", stripped)
        stripped = self.link_pattern.sub("", stripped)
        return stripped

    def embed(self, html_text: str, jsonld_text: str, source: str) -> str:
        """
        embed the given JSON-LD into the given page, replacing an earlier embedding

        Args:
            html_text: the html of a volume page
            jsonld_text: the pretty printed JSON-LD
            source: what the JSON-LD was derived from e.g. the url of the volume

        Returns:
            str: the html with the JSON-LD embedded

        Raises:
            ValueError: if the page has no html or no head element
        """
        stripped = self.strip(html_text)
        html_match = self.html_pattern.search(stripped)
        head_match = self.head_pattern.search(stripped)
        if html_match is None or head_match is None:
            raise ValueError("no html or head element to embed into")
        doctype_match = self.doctype_pattern.match(stripped)
        state_at = doctype_match.end() if doctype_match else html_match.start()
        state_comment = self.state.as_html(source, state="embedded")
        inserted = f"{self.alternate_link}\n{Fence.as_html(jsonld_text)}\n"
        embedded = (
            stripped[:state_at]
            + state_comment
            + "\n"
            + stripped[state_at : head_match.end()]
            + inserted
            + stripped[head_match.end() :]
        )
        return embedded

class SptEndpoint:
    """
    single point of truth endpoint: the JSON-LD files of the site loaded
    into memory on startup and served by the NPQ endpoint of pyLoDStorage,
    see https://cr.bitplan.com/index.php/NPQ-FakeSparql
    """

    def __init__(self, site: Site, name: str = "ceur-ws"):
        """
        constructor

        Args:
            site: the directory tree with the JSON-LD files
            name: the name the graph is served under: /npq/<name>
        """
        self.site = site
        self.name = name
        self.graph = Graph()

    def load(self) -> LoadReport:
        """
        load all JSON-LD files of the site into the graph

        Returns:
            LoadReport: number of files and triples and the time used
        """
        report = LoadReport()
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for path in self.site.jsonld_paths():
            self.graph.parse(path, format="json-ld")
            report.files += 1
        report.triples = len(self.graph)
        report.seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        return report

    def serve(self, host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = 9987) -> None:
        """
        serve the graph over the SPARQL protocol

        Args:
            host: the host to listen on
            port: the port to listen on
        """
        endpoint = NpqEndpoint()
        endpoint.add_graph(self.name, self.graph)
        endpoint.run(host=host, port=port)

class Generator:
    """
    generate the pages of volumes and years of the site
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        site: Site,
        config: SiteConfig,
        mapper: Mapper,
        jsonld: JsonLd,
        spt: CeurSpt,
        state: Optional[PageState] = None,
    ):
        """
        constructor

        Args:
            site: the directory tree to generate into
            config: the site configuration
            mapper: the mapper of the source records to the research model
            jsonld: the JSON-LD support of the research model
            spt: the service that provides the source records
            state: the state the pages announce, generated today if None
        """
        self.site = site
        self.config = config
        self.mapper = mapper
        self.jsonld = jsonld
        self.spt = spt
        self.state = state if state is not None else PageState.today()

    @classmethod
    def of_output(cls, output_dir: str, config: Optional[SiteConfig] = None) -> "Generator":
        """
        create a generator for the given output directory

        Args:
            output_dir: the directory that holds the year directories
            config: the site configuration, the default configuration if None

        Returns:
            Generator: the generator
        """
        if config is None:
            config = SiteConfig.of_yaml()
        jsonld = JsonLd.of_yaml()
        generator = cls(
            site=Site(output_dir, jsonld),
            config=config,
            mapper=Mapper.of_yaml(),
            jsonld=jsonld,
            spt=CeurSpt(config.spt_url),
        )
        return generator

    def fetch_proceedings(self, number: int, report: SiteReport) -> Optional[Proceedings]:
        """
        fetch the source record of the volume with the given number and map
        it to the research model

        Args:
            number: the volume number
            report: the report to add problems to

        Returns:
            Optional[Proceedings]: the proceedings, None if the record could not be fetched
        """
        proceedings = None
        try:
            record = self.spt.volume_record(number)
            result = self.mapper.map_record(record, "Proceedings")
            proceedings = result.target
            for paper in proceedings.papers:
                paper.publishedIn = proceedings.url
            for issue in result.issues:
                report.problems.append(f"Vol-{number}: {issue}")
        except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
            report.problems.append(f"Vol-{number}: {self.spt.volume_url(number)}: {error}")
        return proceedings

    def read_proceedings(self, path: str, report: SiteReport) -> Optional[Proceedings]:
        """
        read the proceedings from the local volume page at the given path, an
        embedded page from its JSON-LD, see issues 33 and 34

        Args:
            path: the index.html of the volume or its directory
            report: the report to add problems to

        Returns:
            Optional[Proceedings]: the proceedings, None if the page could not be read
        """
        if os.path.isdir(path):
            path = os.path.join(path, "index.html")
        proceedings = None
        try:
            volume_html = VolumeHtml.of_file(path, self.config.original_url)
            result = volume_html.proceedings()
            proceedings = result.target
            for paper in proceedings.papers:
                paper.publishedIn = proceedings.url
            for issue in result.issues:
                report.problems.append(f"{path}: {issue}")
        except OSError as error:
            report.problems.append(f"{path}: {error}")
        return proceedings

    def write_volume(self, proceedings: Proceedings, report: SiteReport, volume_dir: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        """
        write the page and the JSON-LD file of the given proceedings

        Args:
            proceedings: the proceedings, with a year
            report: the report to add the written files to
            volume_dir: the directory to write to, the year tree of the site if None
        """
        if volume_dir is None:
            volume_dir = self.site.volume_dir(proceedings)
        page = VolumePage(proceedings, self.config, self.jsonld, self.state)
        self.site.write(os.path.join(volume_dir, "index.html"), page.as_html(), report)
        self.site.write(os.path.join(volume_dir, "index.jsonld"), page.jsonld_text() + "\n", report)
        for paper in proceedings.papers:
            if paper.id:
                self.write_paper(proceedings, paper, report, os.path.join(volume_dir, paper.id))

    def write_paper(self, proceedings: Proceedings, paper: Paper, report: SiteReport, paper_dir: str) -> None:
        """
        write the page and the JSON-LD file of the given paper

        Args:
            proceedings: the proceedings the paper is published in
            paper: the paper, with an id
            report: the report to add the written files to
            paper_dir: the directory to write to
        """
        page = PaperPage(paper, proceedings, self.config, self.jsonld, self.state)
        self.site.write(os.path.join(paper_dir, "index.html"), page.as_html(), report)
        self.site.write(os.path.join(paper_dir, "index.jsonld"), page.jsonld_text() + "\n", report)

    def generate_volumes(self, numbers: List[int], progress: bool = False) -> SiteReport:
        """
        generate the pages of the volumes with the given numbers

        A volume that can not be fetched or has no event start date is not
        written and reported as a problem. Year pages are not touched.

        Args:
            numbers: the volume numbers
            progress: if True show a progress bar

        Returns:
            SiteReport: the written files, the problems and the time used
        """
        report = SiteReport()
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for number in tqdm(numbers, desc="volumes", unit="vol", disable=not progress):
            proceedings = self.fetch_proceedings(number, report)
            if proceedings is None:
                continue
            if proceedings.year() is None:
                report.problems.append(f"Vol-{number}: no event start date, the volume has no year")
                continue
            self.write_volume(proceedings, report)
        report.seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        return report

    def generate_paths(self, paths: List[str], progress: bool = False, in_place: bool = False) -> SiteReport:
        """
        generate the pages of the volumes from their local volume pages
        instead of ceur-spt, see issues 33 and 34; the volume pages are not
        touched unless in_place is set, see issue 43: then the volume page,
        its index.jsonld and the paper pages are written into the volume
        directory itself and the year tree of the site is not used

        A volume that can not be read or has no event start date is not
        written and reported as a problem. Year pages are not touched.

        Args:
            paths: the index.html files of the volumes or their directories
            progress: if True show a progress bar
            in_place: if True write into the volume directories of the given pages

        Returns:
            SiteReport: the written files, the problems and the time used
        """
        report = SiteReport()
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for path in tqdm(paths, desc="volumes", unit="vol", disable=not progress):
            proceedings = self.read_proceedings(path, report)
            if proceedings is None:
                continue
            if proceedings.year() is None:
                report.problems.append(f"{path}: no event start date, the volume has no year")
                continue
            volume_dir = None
            if in_place:
                volume_dir = path if os.path.isdir(path) else os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
            self.write_volume(proceedings, report, volume_dir)
        report.seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        return report

    def rebuild_year(self, year: int) -> SiteReport:
        """
        rebuild the page of the given year from the volumes present for it

        Args:
            year: the year

        Returns:

        the given path and write index.jsonld next to it, see issue 28

        parsed from the embedded page equal the proceedings parsed from the
        original page.

        except OSError as error:

        extracted from the fence of index.html equals index.jsonld

        Args:

def generate_paths(self, paths: List[str], progress: bool = False, in_place: bool = False) -> SiteReport:
    """
    generate the pages of the volumes from their local volume pages
    instead of ceur-spt, see issues 33 and 34; the volume pages are not
    touched unless in_place is set, see issue 43: then the volume page,
    its index.jsonld and the paper pages are written into the volume
    directory itself and the year tree of the site is not used

    A volume that can not be read or has no event start date is not
    written and reported as a problem. Year pages are not touched.

        progress: if True show a progress bar
        in_place: if True write into the volume directories of the given pages

    Returns:

    report = SiteReport()
    start = time.perf_counter()
    for path in tqdm(paths, desc="volumes", unit="vol", disable=not progress):

        if proceedings is None:

        if proceedings.year() is None:

        self.write_volume(proceedings, report, volume_dir)

class JsonLd:
    """
    JSON-LD of the research model according to the context table
    resources/context.yaml
    """

    def __init__(self, table: Dict[str, Any]):
        """
        constructor

        Args:
            table: the context table: namespaces, provisional terms and classes
        """
        self.table = table
        self.classes = table["classes"]

    @classmethod
    def default_table_path(cls) -> str:
        """
        get the path of the context table

        Returns:
            str: the path of resources/context.yaml
        """
        path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "resources", "context.yaml")
        return path

    @classmethod
    def of_yaml(cls, path: Optional[str] = None) -> "JsonLd":
        """
        create the JSON-LD support from the given context table

        Args:
            path: the path of the yaml file, the default table if None

        Returns:
            JsonLd: the JSON-LD support
        """
        if path is None:
            path = cls.default_table_path()
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as table_file:
            table = yaml.safe_load(table_file)
        jsonld = cls(table)
        return jsonld

    def term_definition(self, term: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        get the JSON-LD term definition for the given row of the context table

        Args:
            term: the row: id or reverse, optionally type and container

        Returns:
            Dict[str, Any]: the term definition
        """
        definition = {}
        if "reverse" in term:
            definition["@reverse"] = term["reverse"]
        else:
            definition["@id"] = term["id"]
        if "type" in term:
            definition["@type"] = term["type"]
        if "container" in term:
            definition["@container"] = term["container"]
        return definition

    def context(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        get the JSON-LD context: the namespaces and per class a type scoped
        context with the terms of its fields

        Returns:
            Dict[str, Any]: the value of @context
        """
        context: Dict[str, Any] = {"@version": 1.1}
        context.update(self.table["namespaces"])
        for class_name, class_row in self.classes.items():
            scoped = {}
            for field_name, term in class_row["terms"].items():
                scoped[field_name] = self.term_definition(term)
            context[class_name] = {"@id": class_row["type"], "@context": scoped}
        return context

    def node(self, instance: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        get the JSON-LD node of the given object of the research model

        Fields without value are left out.

        Args:
            instance: the object e.g. a Proceedings

        Returns:
            Dict[str, Any]: the node with @type and, if the class has an id field, @id
        """
        class_name = type(instance).__name__
        class_row = self.classes[class_name]
        node: Dict[str, Any] = {"@type": class_name}
        id_field = class_row.get("id_field")
        if id_field and getattr(instance, id_field):
            node["@id"] = getattr(instance, id_field)
        for field in dataclasses.fields(instance):
            value = getattr(instance, field.name)
            if value is None or value == []:
                continue
            if dataclasses.is_dataclass(value):
                value = self.node(value)
            elif isinstance(value, list):
                value = [self.node(item) for item in value]
            node[field.name] = value
        return node

    def document(self, instance: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        get the JSON-LD document of the given object of the research model

        Args:
            instance: the object e.g. a Proceedings or a Paper

        Returns:
            Dict[str, Any]: the document with @context
        """
        document = {"@context": self.context()}
        document.update(self.node(instance))
        return document

    def as_text(self, instance: Any) -> str:
        """
        get the pretty printed JSON-LD document of the given object

        Args:
            instance: the object e.g. a Proceedings or a Paper

        Returns:
            str: the JSON-LD with an indent of two
        """
        text = json.dumps(self.document(instance), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
        return text

    def plain(self, value: Any) -> Any:
        """
        remove the JSON-LD keywords from the given value

        Args:
            value: a node, a list of nodes or a plain value

        Returns:
            Any: the value without the keys that start with @
        """
        plain = value

def node(self, instance: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    get the JSON-LD node of the given object of the research model

    Fields without value are left out.

    Args:
        instance: the object e.g. a Proceedings

    id_field = class_row.get("id_field")
    if id_field and getattr(instance, id_field):
        node["@id"] = getattr(instance, id_field)
    for field in dataclasses.fields(instance):
        value = getattr(instance, field.name)
        if value is None or value == []:
            continue
        if dataclasses.is_dataclass(value):
            value = self.node(value)

            value = [self.node(item) for item in value]

@dataclass
class LocTime:
    """
    location and time of an event as given in the CEURLOCTIME text of a
    volume page e.g. Verona, Italy, June 8-12, 2026
    """

    text: str
    location: Optional[str] = None
    city: Optional[str] = None
    country: Optional[str] = None
    virtual: bool = False
    startDate: Optional[str] = None
    endDate: Optional[str] = None
    # why the date could not be parsed, None if it was
    message: Optional[str] = None

    MONTH = r"(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)[a-z]*\.?"
    DAY = r"\d{1,2}(?:st|nd|rd|th)?"
    SEP = r"\s*(?:-|–|—|to|until)\s*"
    YEAR = r"\d{4}"
    # the date forms, the most specific first; m: month, d: day, y: year
    DATE_FORMS = [
        # December 30, 2025 - January 2, 2026
        rf"(?P<m1>{MONTH})\s+(?P<d1>{DAY}),?\s+(?P<y1>{YEAR}){SEP}(?P<m2>{MONTH})\s+(?P<d2>{DAY}),?\s+(?P<y2>{YEAR})",
        # September 29 - October 3, 2025
        rf"(?P<m1>{MONTH})\s+(?P<d1>{DAY}){SEP}(?P<m2>{MONTH})\s+(?P<d2>{DAY}),?\s+(?P<y1>{YEAR})",
        # June 8-12, 2026
        rf"(?P<m1>{MONTH})\s+(?P<d1>{DAY}){SEP}(?P<d2>{DAY}),?\s+(?P<y1>{YEAR})",
        # March 1st, 2021
        rf"(?P<m1>{MONTH})\s+(?P<d1>{DAY}),?\s+(?P<y1>{YEAR})",
        # 30 June - 2 July 2026
        rf"(?P<d1>{DAY})\s+(?P<m1>{MONTH}){SEP}(?P<d2>{DAY})\s+(?P<m2>{MONTH}),?\s+(?P<y1>{YEAR})",
        # 1-3 December 2025
        rf"(?P<d1>{DAY}){SEP}(?P<d2>{DAY})\s+(?P<m1>{MONTH}),?\s+(?P<y1>{YEAR})",
        # 3 December 2025
        rf"(?P<d1>{DAY})\s+(?P<m1>{MONTH}),?\s+(?P<y1>{YEAR})",
    ]
    date_patterns = [re.compile(date_form) for date_form in DATE_FORMS]
    virtual_pattern = re.compile(r"\b(online|virtual)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
    months: ClassVar[Dict[str, int]] = {
        "jan": 1,
        "feb": 2,
        "mar": 3,
        "apr": 4,
        "may": 5,
        "jun": 6,
        "jul": 7,
        "aug": 8,
        "sep": 9,
        "oct": 10,
        "nov": 11,
        "dec": 12,
    }

    @classmethod
    def iso_date(cls, year: str, month: str, day: str) -> str:
        """
        get the ISO date of the given parts

        Args:
            year: the four digit year
            month: the month name, full or abbreviated
            day: the day, with an optional ordinal suffix

        Returns:
            str: the date as YYYY-MM-DD

        Raises:
            ValueError: if the parts are not a valid date
        """
        month_number = cls.months[month[:3].lower()]
        day_number = int(re.sub(r"\D", "", day))
        iso_date = date(int(year), month_number, day_number).isoformat()
        return iso_date

    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, text: str) -> "LocTime":
        """
        parse the given location and time text

        The date is the last part of the text; what is before it is the
        location, its first comma separated part the city and its last part
        the country. An online or virtual location has no city and no country.

        Args:
            text: the text e.g. Verona, Italy, June 8-12, 2026

        Returns:
            LocTime: the location and time, with a message if the date could not be parsed
        """
        text = " ".join(text.split())
        loctime = cls(text=text, location=text or None)
        match = None
        for pattern in cls.date_patterns:
            match = pattern.search(text)
            if match:
                break
        if match:
            parts = match.groupdict()
            try:
                loctime.startDate = cls.iso_date(parts["y1"], parts["m1"], parts["d1"])
                end_year = parts.get("y2") or parts["y1"]
                end_month = parts.get("m2") or parts["m1"]
                end_day = parts.get("d2") or parts["d1"]
                loctime.endDate = cls.iso_date(end_year, end_month, end_day)
            except ValueError as error:
                loctime.message = f"invalid date in {text}: {error}"
            loctime.location = text[: match.start()].rstrip(" ,.;") or None
        else:
            loctime.message = f"no date found in {text}" if text else "empty location and time"
        if loctime.location:
            if cls.virtual_pattern.search(loctime.location):
                loctime.virtual = True
            else:
                parts = [part.strip() for part in loctime.location.split(",") if part.strip()]
                loctime.city = parts[0]
                if len(parts) > 1:
                    loctime.country = parts[-1]
        return loctime

class Mapper:
    """
    map source records to the research model as declared in a mapping table
    """

    def __init__(self, mapping: Dict[str, Any]):
        """
        constructor

        Args:
            mapping: the mapping table: per target class the fields and the ignored source keys
        """
        self.mapping = mapping

    @classmethod
    def default_mapping_path(cls) -> str:
        """
        get the path of the mapping table for the JSON-LD of ceur-spt

        Returns:
            str: the path of resources/ceurspt_mapping.yaml
        """
        path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "resources", "ceurspt_mapping.yaml")
        return path

    @classmethod
    def of_yaml(cls, path: Optional[str] = None) -> "Mapper":
        """
        create a mapper from the given mapping table

        Args:
            path: the path of the yaml file, the ceur-spt mapping if None

        Returns:
            Mapper: the mapper
        """
        if path is None:
            path = cls.default_mapping_path()
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as mapping_file:
            mapping = yaml.safe_load(mapping_file)
        mapper = cls(mapping)
        return mapper

    def target_class(self, class_name: str) -> Type:
        """
        get the class of the research model with the given name

        Args:
            class_name: the name of the class e.g. Proceedings

        Returns:
            Type: the class
        """
        target_class = getattr(model, class_name)
        return target_class

    def convert(self, value: Any, rule: Dict[str, Any], result: MappingResult) -> Any:
        """
        convert a source value according to the given rule

        Args:
            value: the source value
            rule: the rule of the mapping table for the target field
            result: the mapping result to add issues to

        Returns:
            Any: the converted value, None if the value could not be converted
        """
        converted = value
        nested_class = rule.get("class")
        conversion = rule.get("as")
        if nested_class:
            converted = self.map_nested(value, nested_class, rule.get("into"), result)
        elif conversion:
            converted = getattr(Convert, conversion)(value)
        return converted

    def map_nested(self, value: Any, class_name: str, into: Optional[str], result: MappingResult) -> Any:
        """
        map a nested source value to an object or a list of objects

        Args:
            value: a source record, a list of source records or a plain value
            class_name: the name of the target class
            into: the field of the target class that takes a plain value
            result: the mapping result to add issues to

        Returns:
            Any: the object or list of objects
        """
        if isinstance(value, list):
            nested = [self.map_nested(item, class_name, into, result) for item in value]
        elif isinstance(value, dict):
            nested_result = self.map_record(value, class_name)
            result.issues.extend(nested_result.issues)
            nested = nested_result.target
        elif into:
            nested = self.target_class(class_name)(**{into: Convert.text(value)})
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"plain value {value} for {class_name} without into field")
        return nested

    def map_record(self, record: Dict[str, Any], class_name: str) -> MappingResult:
        """
        map the given source record to an object of the given class

        Source keys that are neither mapped nor ignored and values that can
        not be converted are reported as issues.

        Args:
            record: the source record
            class_name: the name of the target class e.g. Proceedings

        Returns:
            MappingResult: the object and the issues
        """
        result = MappingResult()
        class_mapping = self.mapping[class_name]
        rules = class_mapping.get("fields") or {}
        ignored = class_mapping.get("ignore") or {}
        values = {}
        mapped_keys = set()
        for target_field, rule in rules.items():
            source_key = rule["from"]
            mapped_keys.add(source_key)
            value = record.get(source_key)
            if value is None or value == "":
                continue
            try:
                values[target_field] = self.convert(value, rule, result)
            except ValueError as error:
                result.issues.append(MappingIssue(class_name, source_key, str(error)))
        for source_key in record:
            if source_key not in mapped_keys and source_key not in ignored:
                result.issues.append(MappingIssue(class_name, source_key, "not in the mapping table"))
        result.target = self.target_class(class_name)(**values)
        return result

def map_record(self, record: Dict[str, Any], class_name: str) -> MappingResult:
    """
    map the given source record to an object of the given class

    Source keys that are neither mapped nor ignored and values that can
    not be converted are reported as issues.

    Args:
        record: the source record
        class_name: the name of the target class e.g. Proceedings

    Returns:
        MappingResult: the object and the issues
    """
    result = MappingResult()
    class_mapping = self.mapping[class_name]
    rules = class_mapping.get("fields") or {}
    ignored = class_mapping.get("ignore") or {}
    values = {}
    mapped_keys = set()
    for target_field, rule in rules.items():
        source_key = rule["from"]
        mapped_keys.add(source_key)
        value = record.get(source_key)
        if value is None or value == "":
            continue
        try:
            values[target_field] = self.convert(value, rule, result)
        except ValueError as error:
            result.issues.append(MappingIssue(class_name, source_key, str(error)))
    for source_key in record:
        if source_key not in mapped_keys and source_key not in ignored:
            result.issues.append(MappingIssue(class_name, source_key, "not in the mapping table"))
    result.target = self.target_class(class_name)(**values)
    return result

class Header:
    """
    the page header: an html snippet outside the code with {{ variable }}
    placeholders that are filled by the parameter handling of pyLoDStorage
    """

    def __init__(self, config: SiteConfig):
        """
        constructor

        Args:
            config: the site configuration with the path of the snippet,
                without a path the header is the title as plain heading
        """
        self.config = config
        self.snippet = """  <h1>{{ title }}</h1>"""
        if config.header:
            with open(config.header, "r", encoding="utf-8") as header_file:
                self.snippet = header_file.read().rstrip("\n")

    def value(self, raw_value: Any) -> str:
        """
        prepare the given value for a placeholder

        Args:
            raw_value: the value

        Returns:
            str: the escaped text; a backslash and an opening brace are given as
                character references since the parameter handling replaces by
                regular expression and a value must not introduce a placeholder
        """
        value = esc(raw_value).replace("\\", "\").replace("{", "{")
        return value

    def values(self, title: str) -> Dict[str, str]:
        """
        get the values of the variables a snippet may use

        Args:
            title: the title of the page

        Returns:
            Dict[str, str]: the escaped value by variable name
        """
        raw_values = {
            "title": title,
            "series_title": self.config.series_title,
            "series_issn": self.config.series_issn,
            "original_url": self.config.original_url,
            "base_url": self.config.base_url,
        }
        values = {name: self.value(raw_value) for name, raw_value in raw_values.items()}
        return values

    def as_html(self, title: str) -> str:
        """
        get the header for the page with the given title

        Args:
            title: the title of the page

        Returns:
            str: the snippet with all placeholders filled

        Raises:
            ValueError: if the snippet uses a variable that is not available
        """
        values = self.values(title)
        # the values are escaped for html, the audit for query parameters does not apply
        params = Params(self.snippet, with_audit=False)
        unknown = sorted(set(params.params) - set(values.keys()))
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"header {self.config.header} uses unknown variables: {', '.join(unknown)}")
        params.set(values)
        header = params.apply_parameters()
        return header

class ScholarView:
    """
    html view of a scholar
    """

    # label, field of the scholar and formatter URI as in CrSchema
    identifier_formatters = [
        ("ORCID", "orcid", "https://orcid.org/$1"),
        ("dblp", "dblpId", "https://dblp.org/pid/$1"),
        ("Wikidata", "wikiDataId", "https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/$1"),

    ]

    def as_html(self, css_class: str) -> str:

        """

            if identifier:
                url = esc(formatter.replace("$1", identifier))
                links.append(f"""<a href="{url}">{label}</a>""")

    def page_url(self) -> str:
        """

    def head_as_html(self) -> str:
        """

        number = esc(self.proceedings.volumeNumber)

        stylesheet = esc(self.config.stylesheet)
        fence = Fence.as_html(self.jsonld_text())
        head = f"""<head>

  <link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="{stylesheet}">
  <link rel="alternate" type="application/ld+json" href="index.jsonld">
  <title>CEUR-WS.org/Vol-{number} - {title}</title>
{fence}
</head>"""
        return head

    def links_as_html(self) -> str:
        """
        get the links to the original volume, its copy and the year

        Returns:
            str: the html paragraph
        """
        number = esc(self.proceedings.volumeNumber)
        year = esc(self.proceedings.year())
        original_url = esc(self.original_url())
        base_url = esc(self.config.base_url)
        links = f"""  <p class="unobtrusive">Original: <a href="{original_url}">{original_url}</a> |
    Mirror: <a href="/Vol-{number}/">{base_url}/Vol-{number}/</a> |
    Year: <a href="../">{year}</a></p>"""
        return links

    def header_as_html(self) -> str:
        """
        get the header with volume number, URN and copyright

        Returns:
            str: the html table
        """
        number = esc(self.proceedings.volumeNumber)
        urn = esc(self.proceedings.urn)
        pub_year = esc(self.proceedings.pubYear)
        license_url = esc(self.proceedings.license)
        doi = doi_as_html(self.proceedings.doi)
        if doi:
            doi = f""" <br>
          {doi}"""
        header = f"""  <table style="border: 0; border-spacing: 0; border-collapse: collapse; width: 95%">
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <td style="text-align: left; vertical-align: middle">
          <a href="../"><div id="CEURWSLOGO"></div></a>
        </td>
        <td style="text-align: right; vertical-align: middle">
          <span class="CEURVOLNR">Vol-{number}</span> <br>
          <span class="CEURURN">{urn}</span>{doi}
          <p class="unobtrusive copyright" style="text-align: justify">Copyright © {pub_year} for
            the individual papers by the papers' authors.
            Copyright © <span class="CEURPUBYEAR">{pub_year}</span> for the volume
            as a collection by its editors.
            This volume and its papers are published under
            <a href="{license_url}"><span class="CEURLIC">{license_url}</span></a>.
          </p>
        </td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>"""
        return header

    def acronym_as_html(self) -> str:
        """
        get the acronym of the event, linked to its homepage if there is one

        Returns:
            str: the html span or link
        """
        event = self.proceedings.event
        acronym = esc(event.acronym)
        acronym_html = f"""<span class="CEURVOLACRONYM">{acronym}</span>"""
        if event.homepage:
            homepage = esc(event.homepage)
            acronym_html = f"""<a href="{homepage}">{acronym_html}</a>"""
        return acronym_html

    def colocated_as_html(self) -> str:
        """
        get the event the event of the proceedings is co-located with

        Returns:
            str: the html text, empty if the event is not co-located
        """
        colocated_html = ""
        colocated_with = self.proceedings.event.colocated_with
        if colocated_with:
            acronym = esc(colocated_with.acronym)
            colocated_html = f"""<br>
    co-located with <span class="CEURCOLOCATED">{acronym}</span>"""
        return colocated_html

        """

            str: the html headings
        """
        acronym = self.acronym_as_html()
        title = esc(self.proceedings.title)
        colocated = self.colocated_as_html()
        location = esc(self.proceedings.event.location)
        title_html = f"""  <h1>{acronym}</h1>

        state = self.state.as_html("the embedded JSON-LD")
        head = self.head_as_html()
        links = self.links_as_html()
        header = self.header_as_html()
        title = self.title_as_html()
        editors = self.editors_as_html()
        toc = self.toc_as_html()
        footer = self.footer_as_html()

{state}

{head}

{links}

{header}

{title}

{editors}

class CeurSpt:
    """
    access to the JSON-LD of volumes as served by ceur-spt
    """

    def __init__(self, spt_url: str, timeout: float = 60.0):
        """
        constructor

        Args:
            spt_url: the base url of the service, http, https or file
            timeout: the time in seconds to wait for an answer
        """
        self.spt_url = spt_url.rstrip("/")
        self.timeout = timeout
        # one session for all requests so that the connection is kept alive
        self.session = requests.Session()

    def volume_url(self, number: int) -> str:
        """
        get the url of the JSON-LD of the volume with the given number

        Args:
            number: the volume number

        Returns:
            str: the url
        """
        volume_url = f"{self.spt_url}/Vol-{number}.jsonld"
        return volume_url

    def volume_text(self, number: int) -> str:
        """
        fetch the text of the JSON-LD of the volume with the given number

        Args:
            number: the volume number

        Returns:
            str: the text

        Raises:
            OSError: if the service does not answer or answers with an error
        """
        volume_url = self.volume_url(number)
        if volume_url.startswith("file://"):
            with urllib.request.urlopen(volume_url, timeout=self.timeout) as response:
                text = response.read().decode("utf-8")
        else:
            response = self.session.get(volume_url, timeout=self.timeout)
            response.raise_for_status()
            text = response.text
        return text

    def volume_record(self, number: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        fetch the JSON-LD of the volume with the given number

        Args:
            number: the volume number

        Returns:
            Dict[str, Any]: the JSON-LD document

        Raises:
            OSError: if the service does not answer or answers with an error
            ValueError: if the answer is not JSON
        """
        record = json.loads(self.volume_text(number))
        return record

    def year_dir(self, year: int) -> str:
        """

        """
        year_dir = os.path.join(self.root, str(year))
        return year_dir

    def volume_dir(self, proceedings: Proceedings) -> str:
        """
        get the directory of the given proceedings

        Args:
            proceedings: the proceedings, with a year and a volume number

        Returns:
            str: the path
        """
        volume_dir = os.path.join(self.year_dir(proceedings.year()), f"Vol-{proceedings.volumeNumber}")
        return volume_dir

    def paper_dir(self, proceedings: Proceedings, paper_id: str) -> str:
        """
        get the directory of the paper with the given id

        Args:
            proceedings: the proceedings the paper is published in
            paper_id: the id of the paper e.g. paper1

        Returns:
            str: the path
        """
        paper_dir = os.path.join(self.volume_dir(proceedings), paper_id)
        return paper_dir

    def write(self, path: str, content: str, report: SiteReport) -> None:
        """
        write the given content to the given file

        Args:
            path: the path of the file
            content: the content
            report: the report to add the path to
        """
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as out_file:
            out_file.write(content)

        Returns:
            List[str]: the sorted paths of the index.jsonld files
        """

        pattern = os.path.join(self.root, year_pattern, "Vol-*", "index.jsonld")

    def volume_numbers(self, year: int) -> List[int]:
        """
        get the numbers of the volumes that are present for the given year

        Args:

    def read_proceedings(self, path: str) -> Proceedings:

        read the proceedings of the given JSON-LD file

        Args:

        Returns:
            Proceedings: the proceedings
        """

            document = json.load(jsonld_file)

        return proceedings

    def proceedings_of_year(self, year: int) -> List[Proceedings]:
        """
        get the proceedings that are present for the given year

        Args:
            year: the year

        Returns:
            List[Proceedings]: the proceedings
        """
        proceedings_list = [self.read_proceedings(path) for path in self.jsonld_paths(year)]
        return proceedings_list

    def years(self) -> List[int]:
        """
        get the years that have a directory

        Returns:
            List[int]: the sorted years
        """
        years = []
        if os.path.isdir(self.root):
            years = sorted(int(name) for name in os.listdir(self.root) if name.isdigit() and len(name) == 4)
        return years

    volume numbers given as numbers and ranges e.g. 3889 3887-3912

    @classmethod
    def numbers(cls, ranges: List[str]) -> List[int]:
        """
        get the volume numbers of the given numbers and ranges

        Args:
            ranges: numbers such as 3889 and ranges such as 3887-3912

        Returns:
            List[int]: the sorted volume numbers without duplicates

        Raises:
            ValueError: if a range is not a number or two numbers separated by a hyphen
        """
        numbers = set()
        for volume_range in ranges:
            parts = volume_range.split("-")
            if len(parts) > 2 or not all(part.isdigit() for part in parts):
                raise ValueError(f"not a volume number or range: {volume_range}")
            first = int(parts[0])
            last = int(parts[-1])
            if last < first:
                raise ValueError(f"range ends before it starts: {volume_range}")
            numbers.update(range(first, last + 1))
        sorted_numbers = sorted(numbers)
        return sorted_numbers

class VolumeHtml:
    """
    a volume page with the CEUR* marks of the volume template
    """

    publisher_name = "CEUR-WS.org"
    # tried after the declared charset; latin-1 decodes every byte
    fallback_encodings = ["utf-8", "cp1252", "latin-1"]
    # an embedded page announces its state and carries its JSON-LD in a fence with a marker line, see issue 28
    embedded_pattern = re.compile(r"<!-- CEURSTATE=embedded[^\n]*-->")
    fence_pattern = re.compile(r"```json-ld\n(?:[^\n{\[]*\n)?(.*?)\n```", re.DOTALL)
    _jsonld: Optional[JsonLd] = None

    def __init__(self, text: str, base_url: str = "https://ceur-ws.org", volume_number: Optional[int] = None):
        """
        constructor

        Args:
            text: the html of the volume page
            base_url: the url of the site the volume is published on
            volume_number: the number of the volume for pages without CEURVOLNR
        """
        self.text = text
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self.volume_number = volume_number
        self.soup = BeautifulSoup(text, "html.parser")
        self.issues: List[MappingIssue] = []
        self.embedded = False
        self.jsonld_document: Optional[dict] = None

    @classmethod
    def jsonld(cls) -> JsonLd:
        """
        the JSON-LD support of the research model, loaded once
        """
        if cls._jsonld is None:
            cls._jsonld = JsonLd.of_yaml()
        return cls._jsonld

    def read_embedded(self, path: str) -> None:
        """
        read the JSON-LD of an embedded page, the source of the mapping instead of the markup, see issue 28:
        index.jsonld beside the page is the record that the DOI registration writes, see issue 42;
        the fence of the page is the copy and is read only when there is no index.jsonld

        Args:
            path: the path of the index.html
        """
        if not self.embedded_pattern.search(self.text):
            return
        self.embedded = True
        document = None
        jsonld_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(path), "index.jsonld")
        if os.path.isfile(jsonld_path):
            with open(jsonld_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as jsonld_file:
                document = json.load(jsonld_file)
        else:
            match = self.fence_pattern.search(self.text)
            if match and match.group(1).strip():
                document = json.loads(match.group(1))
        if document is None:
            self.issues.append(
                MappingIssue(
                    "Proceedings", "CEURSTATE", "embedded, but neither the fence nor index.jsonld holds the JSON-LD"
                )
            )
        self.jsonld_document = document

    @classmethod
    def decode(cls, raw: bytes) -> Tuple[str, Optional[str], str]:
        """
        decode the bytes of a volume page with its declared charset,
        then with the fallback encodings, see https://github.com/ceurws/semantify/issues/38

        Args:
            raw: the bytes of the page

        Returns:
            Tuple[str, Optional[str], str]: the text, the declared charset or None and the encoding used
        """
        match = re.search(rb"charset\s*=\s*[\"']?([A-Za-z0-9_.:\-]+)", raw[:4096], re.IGNORECASE)
        declared = match.group(1).decode("ascii") if match else None
        encodings = ([declared] if declared else []) + cls.fallback_encodings
        text = None
        used = None
        for encoding in encodings:
            try:
                text = raw.decode(encoding)
                used = encoding
                break
            except (LookupError, UnicodeDecodeError):
                pass
        return text, declared, used

    @classmethod
    def of_file(cls, path: str, base_url: str = "https://ceur-ws.org") -> "VolumeHtml":
        """
        read the volume page from the given file

        Args:
            path: the path of the index.html, the volume number is taken from a Vol-N part of it
            base_url: the url of the site the volume is published on

        Returns:
            VolumeHtml: the volume page, an EarlyVolumeHtml for a page without CEURVOLNR
        """
        with open(path, "rb") as html_file:
            raw = html_file.read()
        text, declared, used = cls.decode(raw)
        numbers = re.findall(r"Vol-(\d+)", path)
        volume_number = int(numbers[-1]) if numbers else None
        volume_class = cls
        if "CEURVOLNR" not in text:
            # imported here since the early volume page is a subclass of this one
            from ceursemantify.early_volume_html import EarlyVolumeHtml

            volume_class = EarlyVolumeHtml
        volume_html = volume_class(text, base_url, volume_number)
        volume_html.read_embedded(path)
        expected = (declared or "utf-8").lower().replace("-", "")
        if used.lower().replace("-", "") != expected:
            volume_html.issues.append(MappingIssue("Proceedings", "charset", f"declared {declared}, decoded as {used}"))
        return volume_html

    def mark(self, css_class: str, root: Optional[Tag] = None) -> Optional[Tag]:
        """
        get the first element with the given CEUR mark

        Args:
            css_class: the mark e.g. CEURVOLNR
            root: the element to search in, the whole page if None

        Returns:
            Optional[Tag]: the element, None if there is none
        """
        root = root if root is not None else self.soup
        element = root.find(class_=css_class)
        return element

    def mark_text(self, css_class: str, root: Optional[Tag] = None) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        get the text of the first element with the given CEUR mark

        Args:
            css_class: the mark e.g. CEURVOLNR
            root: the element to search in, the whole page if None

        Returns:
            Optional[str]: the single line text, None if there is no element or no text
        """
        text = None
        element = self.mark(css_class, root)
        if element is not None:
            text = Convert.text(element.get_text()) or None
        return text

    def link_of(self, element: Optional[Tag]) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        get the href of the link the given element is or is wrapped in

        Args:
            element: the element

        Returns:
            Optional[str]: the href, None if the element is not linked
        """
        href = None
        if element is not None:
            link = element if element.name == "a" else element.find_parent("a")
            if link is not None:
                href = link.get("href")
        return href

    def required(self, css_class: str, result: MappingResult) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        get the text of a mark that every volume page must have

        Args:
            css_class: the mark
            result: the mapping result to report a missing mark to

        Returns:
            Optional[str]: the text, None if the mark is missing
        """
        text = self.mark_text(css_class)
        if text is None:
            result.issues.append(MappingIssue("Proceedings", css_class, "mark missing"))
        return text

    def event(self, result: MappingResult) -> Event:
        """
        get the event of the volume

        Args:
            result: the mapping result to report issues to

        Returns:
            Event: the event
        """
        acronym_element = self.mark("CEURVOLACRONYM")
        event = Event(
            acronym=self.mark_text("CEURVOLACRONYM"),
            title=self.mark_text("CEURVOLTITLE"),
            homepage=self.link_of(acronym_element),
        )
        colocated = self.mark_text("CEURCOLOCATED")
        if colocated:
            event.colocated_with = Event(acronym=colocated)
        loctime_text = self.required("CEURLOCTIME", result)
        if loctime_text:
            loctime = LocTime.parse(loctime_text)
            # the full text as ceur-spt has it; place, city and country are derived
            event.location = loctime.text
            event.startDate = loctime.startDate
            event.endDate = loctime.endDate
            if loctime.virtual:
                event.virtual = True
            if loctime.city:
                event.city = City(name=loctime.city)
            if loctime.country:
                event.country = Country(name=loctime.country)
            if loctime.message:
                result.issues.append(MappingIssue("Event", "CEURLOCTIME", loctime.message))
        return event

    def scholar(self, element: Tag) -> Scholar:
        """
        get the scholar of the given CEURVOLEDITOR or CEURAUTHOR element

        Args:
            element: the element with the name, optionally linked to an ORCID

        Returns:
            Scholar: the scholar
        """
        scholar = Scholar.of_full_name(element.get_text())
        for url in [element.get("itemid"), self.link_of(element)]:
            if url and "orcid.org/" in url:
                scholar.orcid = url.rstrip("/").rsplit("/", 1)[1]
                break
        return scholar

    def editors(self) -> List[Scholar]:
        """
        get the editors of the volume

        Returns:
            List[Scholar]: the editors in the order of the page
        """
        editors = [self.scholar(element) for element in self.soup.find_all(class_="CEURVOLEDITOR")]
        return editors

    def paper(self, item: Tag, url: str, result: MappingResult) -> Optional[Paper]:
        """
        get the paper of the given table of contents item

        Args:
            item: the li element of the paper, the id of the paper is the li id
                or the stem of the pdf link when the li has no id
                see https://github.com/ceurws/semantify/issues/36
            url: the url of the volume
            result: the mapping result to report issues to

        Returns:
            Optional[Paper]: the paper, None if the item has no link to a pdf,
                has no id and links to a pdf outside the volume,
                or links to a pdf outside the volume directory: a paper published elsewhere,
                see https://github.com/ceurws/semantify/issues/35
        """
        paper = None
        link = item.find("a", href=lambda href: href and href.lower().endswith(".pdf"))
        paper_id = item.get("id")
        if link is not None and not paper_id:
            href = link["href"]
            # without li id only a pdf of the volume itself is taken
            if not urlparse(href).scheme and "/" not in href.strip("./"):
                paper_id = posixpath.splitext(posixpath.basename(href))[0]
        if link is not None and paper_id:
            pdf_url = urljoin(url, link["href"])
            if not self.in_volume(pdf_url, url):
                result.issues.append(MappingIssue("Paper", paper_id, f"published elsewhere: {pdf_url}"))
            else:
                title = self.mark_text("CEURTITLE", item) or Convert.text(link.get_text()) or None
                if title is None:
                    result.issues.append(MappingIssue("Paper", paper_id, "no title"))
                paper = Paper(
                    id=paper_id,
                    title=title,
                    pdfUrl=pdf_url,
                    publishedIn=url,
                    authors=[self.scholar(element) for element in item.find_all(class_="CEURAUTHOR")],
                )
                pages = self.mark_text("CEURPAGES", item)
                if pages:
                    paper.pageStart = Convert.page_start(pages)
                    paper.pageEnd = Convert.page_end(pages)
        return paper

    @classmethod
    def in_volume(cls, pdf_url: str, url: str) -> bool:
        """
        check whether the given pdf lies in the directory of the volume,
        the criterion for a paper of the volume, see https://github.com/ceurws/semantify/issues/35;
        the scheme is ignored so that http links to an https site still count

        Args:
            pdf_url: the absolute url of the pdf
            url: the url of the volume

        Returns:
            bool: True if the pdf is in the volume directory or one of its subdirectories
        """
        pdf_parts = urlparse(pdf_url)
        volume_parts = urlparse(url)
        in_volume = pdf_parts.netloc == volume_parts.netloc and pdf_parts.path.startswith(volume_parts.path)
        return in_volume

    def papers(self, url: str, result: MappingResult) -> List[Paper]:
        """
        get the papers of the volume

        Args:
            url: the url of the volume
            result: the mapping result to report issues to

        Returns:
            List[Paper]: the papers in the order of the table of contents
        """
        toc = self.mark("CEURTOC") or self.soup
        papers = []
        pdf_urls = set()
        for item in toc.find_all("li"):
            paper = self.paper(item, url, result)
            # an li around a nested list finds the pdf of its first child again
            if paper is not None and paper.pdfUrl not in pdf_urls:
                pdf_urls.add(paper.pdfUrl)
                papers.append(paper)
        return papers

    def volume_number_of(self, result: MappingResult) -> Optional[int]:
        """
        get the volume number of the CEURVOLNR mark

        Args:
            result: the mapping result to report a missing or unparsed mark to

        Returns:
            Optional[int]: the volume number, None if the mark is missing or unparsed
        """
        volume_number = None
        volume_mark = self.required("CEURVOLNR", result)
        if volume_mark:
            try:
                volume_number = Convert.volume_number(volume_mark)
            except ValueError as error:
                result.issues.append(MappingIssue("Proceedings", "CEURVOLNR", str(error)))
        return volume_number

    def proceedings(self) -> MappingResult:
        """
        map the volume page to the proceedings of the research model

        Returns:
            MappingResult: the proceedings and the issues
        """
        result = MappingResult()
        result.issues.extend(self.issues)
        if self.jsonld_document is not None:
            result.target = self.jsonld().proceedings(self.jsonld_document)
            return result
        proceedings = Proceedings(publisher=Publisher(name=self.publisher_name))
        proceedings.volumeNumber = self.volume_number_of(result)
        if proceedings.volumeNumber is not None:
            proceedings.url = f"{self.base_url}/Vol-{proceedings.volumeNumber}/"
            proceedings.archive = f"{self.base_url}/ftp-dir/Vol-{proceedings.volumeNumber}.zip"
        proceedings.urn = self.required("CEURURN", result)
        proceedings.title = self.required("CEURFULLTITLE", result) or self.mark_text("CEURVOLTITLE")
        pub_date = self.required("CEURPUBDATE", result)
        if pub_date:
            try:
                proceedings.pubDate = Convert.iso_date(pub_date)
            except ValueError as error:
                result.issues.append(MappingIssue("Proceedings", "CEURPUBDATE", str(error)))
        pub_year = self.mark_text("CEURPUBYEAR")
        if pub_year:
            try:
                proceedings.pubYear = Convert.integer(pub_year)
            except ValueError as error:
                result.issues.append(MappingIssue("Proceedings", "CEURPUBYEAR", str(error)))
        license_element = self.mark("CEURLIC")
        if license_element is not None:
            proceedings.license = self.link_of(license_element) or self.mark_text("CEURLIC")
        proceedings.event = self.event(result)
        proceedings.editors = self.editors()
        if proceedings.url:
            proceedings.papers = self.papers(proceedings.url, result)
        result.target = proceedings
        return result

@classmethod
def decode(cls, raw: bytes) -> Tuple[str, Optional[str], str]:
    """
    decode the bytes of a volume page with its declared charset,
    then with the fallback encodings, see https://github.com/ceurws/semantify/issues/38

    Args:
        raw: the bytes of the page

    Returns:
        Tuple[str, Optional[str], str]: the text, the declared charset or None and the encoding used
    """
    match = re.search(rb"charset\s*=\s*[\"']?([A-Za-z0-9_.:\-]+)", raw[:4096], re.IGNORECASE)
    declared = match.group(1).decode("ascii") if match else None
    encodings = ([declared] if declared else []) + cls.fallback_encodings
    text = None
    used = None
    for encoding in encodings:
        try:
            text = raw.decode(encoding)
            used = encoding
            break
        except (LookupError, UnicodeDecodeError):
            pass
    return text, declared, used

@classmethod
def of_file(cls, path: str, base_url: str = "https://ceur-ws.org") -> "VolumeHtml":
    """
    read the volume page from the given file

    Args:
        path: the path of the index.html, the volume number is taken from a Vol-N part of it
        base_url: the url of the site the volume is published on

    Returns:
        VolumeHtml: the volume page, an EarlyVolumeHtml for a page without CEURVOLNR
    """
    with open(path, "rb") as html_file:
        raw = html_file.read()
    text, declared, used = cls.decode(raw)
    numbers = re.findall(r"Vol-(\d+)", path)
    volume_number = int(numbers[-1]) if numbers else None
    volume_class = cls
    if "CEURVOLNR" not in text:
        # imported here since the early volume page is a subclass of this one
        from ceursemantify.early_volume_html import EarlyVolumeHtml

        volume_class = EarlyVolumeHtml
    volume_html = volume_class(text, base_url, volume_number)
    volume_html.read_embedded(path)
    expected = (declared or "utf-8").lower().replace("-", "")
    if used.lower().replace("-", "") != expected:
        volume_html.issues.append(MappingIssue("Proceedings", "charset", f"declared {declared}, decoded as {used}"))
    return volume_html

def paper(self, item: Tag, url: str, result: MappingResult) -> Optional[Paper]:
    """
    get the paper of the given table of contents item

    Args:
        item: the li element of the paper, the id of the paper is the li id
            or the stem of the pdf link when the li has no id
            see https://github.com/ceurws/semantify/issues/36
        url: the url of the volume
        result: the mapping result to report issues to

    Returns:
        Optional[Paper]: the paper, None if the item has no link to a pdf,
            has no id and links to a pdf outside the volume,
            or links to a pdf outside the volume directory: a paper published elsewhere,
            see https://github.com/ceurws/semantify/issues/35
    """
    paper = None
    link = item.find("a", href=lambda href: href and href.lower().endswith(".pdf"))
    paper_id = item.get("id")
    if link is not None and not paper_id:
        href = link["href"]
        # without li id only a pdf of the volume itself is taken
        if not urlparse(href).scheme and "/" not in href.strip("./"):
            paper_id = posixpath.splitext(posixpath.basename(href))[0]
    if link is not None and paper_id:
        pdf_url = urljoin(url, link["href"])
        if not self.in_volume(pdf_url, url):
            result.issues.append(MappingIssue("Paper", paper_id, f"published elsewhere: {pdf_url}"))
        else:
            title = self.mark_text("CEURTITLE", item) or Convert.text(link.get_text()) or None
            if title is None:
                result.issues.append(MappingIssue("Paper", paper_id, "no title"))
            paper = Paper(
                id=paper_id,
                title=title,
                pdfUrl=pdf_url,
                publishedIn=url,
                authors=[self.scholar(element) for element in item.find_all(class_="CEURAUTHOR")],
            )
            pages = self.mark_text("CEURPAGES", item)
            if pages:
                paper.pageStart = Convert.page_start(pages)
                paper.pageEnd = Convert.page_end(pages)
    return paper

def read_embedded(self, path: str) -> None:
    """
    read the JSON-LD of an embedded page, the source of the mapping instead of the markup, see issue 28:
    index.jsonld beside the page is the record that the DOI registration writes, see issue 42;
    the fence of the page is the copy and is read only when there is no index.jsonld

    Args:
        path: the path of the index.html
    """
    if not self.embedded_pattern.search(self.text):
        return
    self.embedded = True
    document = None
    jsonld_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(path), "index.jsonld")
    if os.path.isfile(jsonld_path):
        with open(jsonld_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as jsonld_file:
            document = json.load(jsonld_file)
    else:
        match = self.fence_pattern.search(self.text)
        if match and match.group(1).strip():
            document = json.loads(match.group(1))
    if document is None:
        self.issues.append(
            MappingIssue(
                "Proceedings", "CEURSTATE", "embedded, but neither the fence nor index.jsonld holds the JSON-LD"
            )
        )
    self.jsonld_document = document
